fullPassage: [P01] I have often counseled people who were afflicted by their need to be perfect. I have come to learn that their pursuit of perfection is really a disguise for their insecurity. They typically received messages earlier in life that they weren't good enough. So they decided that only by being perfect would they be beyond reproach. With such an affliction we might look at perfectionism as a compensation for earlier life experiences that spoiled someone's well-being and self-esteem. As a compensatory response, the drive toward perfection is sought as a solution. Perfectionists tend to think that other people are somehow better or superior to them, so they need to be without flaw just to catch up. [P02] Although the countries of the industrialized world are now more energy-efficient than they were a century ago, this has not stopped a massive increase in energy consumption. Indeed, there is plenty of evidence that increasing energy efficiency tends to lower energy, particularly electricity, prices (especially in real terms) and this encourages greater use of energy. The experience of the United States in the last two decades of the 20th century illustrates this factor very well. The energy intensity of the US economy fell by 34% in this period. Combined with a population rise of 22%, this should have produced a fall in energy use. However, GDP per head rose by 55%, and so the total amount of energy consumed rose by 26%. Across the world it seems highly unlikely that this pattern will change in the future. Further increases in energy efficiencies through new technologies will not stop the rising demand for energy and even higher energy consumption.

det.korean: 괴로워하는 — 위장 — 비난

questions.passage: [P01] I have often counseled people who were <u>afflicted</u> by their need to be perfect. I have come to learn that their pursuit of perfection is really a disguise for their insecurity. They typically received messages earlier in life that they weren't good enough. So they decided that only by being perfect would they be beyond reproach. With such an affliction we might look at perfectionism as a compensation for earlier life experiences that spoiled someone's well-being and self-esteem. As a compensatory response, the drive toward perfection is sought as a solution. Perfectionists tend to think that other people are somehow better or superior to them, so they need to be without flaw just to catch up. [P02] Although the countries of the industrialized world are now more energy-efficient than they were a century ago, this has not stopped a massive increase in energy consumption. Indeed, there is plenty of evidence that increasing energy efficiency tends to lower energy, particularly electricity, prices (especially in real terms) and this encourages greater use of energy. The experience of the United States in the last two decades of the 20th century illustrates this factor very well. The energy intensity of the US economy fell by 34% in this period. Combined with a population rise of 22%, this should have produced a fall in energy use. However, GDP per head rose by 55%, and so the total amount of energy consumed rose by 26%. Across the world it seems highly unlikely that this pattern will change in the future. Further increases in energy efficiencies through new technologies will not stop the rising demand for energy and even higher energy consumption.

questions.passage:
(A) As a compensatory response, the <u>drive</u> toward perfection is sought as a solution.

(B) After the long night shift, he was too exhausted to <u>drive</u> home safely.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 (A)의 밑줄 친 drive와 (B)의 drive의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 완벽을 향한 욕구 (B) 차를 운전하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) drive = '욕구/충동'(완벽을 향한 강한 욕구), (B) drive = '운전하다'(피곤해서 집까지 운전하기 힘듦)로 두 문맥 모두에 적절 ←정답
❌ ② (A)의 '운전하다'는 명사 자리라 맞지 않음
❌ ③ (B)의 '가축을 몰다'는 집으로 운전해 간다는 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ④ (A)의 '도로'는 '완벽을 향한 도로'라는 어색한 해석이 됨
det.tip: drive: (A) 명사 = 욕구/추진력 (the drive toward perfection). (B) 동사 = 운전하다 (drive home).

❌ ② reduction(감소)은 사용이 아니라 '줄이는' 것
✅ ③ consumption(소비): '에너지 등 자원을 사용하는 행위'라는 정의에 정확히 맞음 ←정답
❌ ④ distribution(분배)은 사용이 아니라 '나누는' 것
det.tip: consumption = 소비. energy consumption = 에너지 소비.

questions.passage: As a compensatory response, the drive toward perfection is __________ (seek) as a solution. Perfectionists tend to think that other people are somehow better or superior to them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 보상 반응으로서, 완벽을 향한 욕구가 하나의 해결책으로 추구된다.
det.analysis: 'be동사(is) + 과거분사 + as ~' 형태의 수동태 구문이다. 주어 the drive가 '추구되는' 대상이므로 seek을 과거분사 sought로 바꿔 'is sought as(~로 추구된다)'를 만든다. seek–sought–sought의 불규칙 변화이고, 수동태라 형태가 유일하게 결정된다.
det.tip: is + 과거분사 = 수동태. seek → sought. the drive is sought as a solution = 욕구가 해결책으로 추구된다.

questions.passage: The energy intensity of the US economy fell by 34% in this period. Combined with a population rise of 22%, this should have __________ (produce) a fall in energy use.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 미국 경제의 에너지 집약도는 이 기간에 34% 떨어졌다. 22%의 인구 증가와 결합되어, 이것은 에너지 사용의 감소를 낳았어야 했다.
det.analysis: 'should have + 과거분사' 형태의 조동사 완료형 구문이다. '~했어야 했다(그런데 실제로는 아니었다)'라는 의미를 만들려면 produce를 과거분사 produced로 바꿔 'should have produced'로 써야 한다. 조동사 have 뒤이므로 형태가 유일하게 결정된다.
det.tip: should have + p.p. = ~했어야 했다. produce → produced. this should have produced a fall = 감소를 낳았어야 했다.
